subject: Dedicated capacity: H100 / A100 / L4 tradeoffs and pilot plan

Subject: Dedicated capacity planning - our workload profile and ask

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited to proceed toward a committed Dedicated plan, but before procurement we need concrete guidance on how to size and split GPU SKUs for our mix:

- Production chat (latency SLO 150ms p95, lots of short sessions, heavy KV caching)
- Long-context RAG agents (8k-32k token contexts, memory-heavy, fewer concurrent sessions)
- High-throughput embeddings (batch and streaming embeddings; cost sensitivity)
- Overnight batch jobs for model finetuning and evaluation (high throughput, flexible latency)

Attached are 72 hours of traces and a sample token distribution (vertice_workload_samples_v3.csv). High-level asks: recommended SKU mix (H100 vs A100 vs L4), reserve vs burst sizing for first 6 months, and a quick note on migration/fallback patterns if we need to shift load.

Procurement (procure@vertice.ai) is cc'd — they'd like an estimate we can plug into the SOW.

Appreciate a short write-up we can review internally.

Carlos

Carlos / team — I ran a quick capacity sketch against the sample traces. Below are the assumptions and a pragmatic SKU split for an initial reserved pool with burst:

Assumptions (from traces):
- Peak concurrent chat sessions: 1,200 short-lived sessions, median 12 tokens per request, p95 40 tokens. Target p95 latency: 150ms.
- Active long-context RAG sessions: 120 concurrently, avg context stored in KV per session 22GB (8k-32k token windows).
- Embedding throughput: sustained 45k vectors/hour with 1.6ms per vector on optimized L4 codepath.
- Overnight batch: flexible, can use burst or spot capacity.

Initial recommendation (reserve + burst):
- Reserve: 10 H100 GPUs (latency-critical chat frontends). Rationale: H100 with high memory-bandwidth and Tensor Cores keeps p95 low for small token bursts and supports high-concurrency tiling when combined with efficient batching.
- Reserve: 8 A100 80GB GPUs (long-context RAG). Rationale: 80GB VRAM avoids OOM for 32k token windows with KV prefetching; higher memory per device reduces tiling complexity and improves endpoint stability.
- Reserve: 12 L4 GPUs (embedding/low-cost inference). Rationale: L4 offers very low cost per token for embeddings and emergent shallow models; reserve enough to handle steady embedding throughput with headroom.
- Burst pool (autoscale): allow up to +40% capacity across H100/A100/L4 for traffic spikes; implement pre-warm policy to avoid cold-start latency for chat.

Concurrency math (back-of-envelope):
- Chat: assume 150ms p95 target => with 10 H100s and efficient micro-batching we estimate ~1600 qps aggregate capacity (buffers and KV cache hit target 90%); that covers peak with headroom.
- RAG: each A100 80GB can host ~9 large-context sessions (with model shard + KV); 8 A100 ~=72 concurrent large contexts — initial gap vs target 120 requires either: increase A100 reserve or rely on burst capacity + request-level shedding to L4-quantized variants for non-critical queries.

Operational notes (Irene/Jasmine to validate):
- KV cache warmers for chat to hit >85% cache-hit at steady state.
- Fallthrough policy: route low-criticality RAG queries to quantized A100 or L4 when memory pressure >85%; this keeps service available albeit with slightly reduced quality.
- Pre-deployment benchmark: we recommend a 48-hour pilot on subset traffic to validate p95 and cost per token.

Attachments: quick sizing spreadsheet (see attached CSV) and the placeholder proposal. I'll hand off ops runbook bullets to Irene.

Cheers,
PrIyom Das

Team — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few quick clarifications before Procurement moves to SOW:

1) For the RAG gap (72 -> 120 concurrent large contexts) can you provide two buy options: (A) increase A100 reserve to cover all 120; (B) keep reserve as proposed and accept a 20% request fallthrough to quantized L4 for non-critical jobs. We need ballpark $/month for both.

2) What is the expected monthly cost delta if we replace 2 H100s with 4 L4s and move low-criticality chat to L4? We're sensitive to committed spend but want to preserve p95 for core flows.

3) Timeline: Procurement needs a MAP with milestones (signature -> infra provision -> pilot window -> production cutover). Can you include a target SLA for p95 and a pre-approved maintenance window that won't trigger credit events?

If you can add quick line items for both options (A) and (B) and a recommended default, Procurement can draft the SOW. If feasible, I can join a 30-min call tomorrow to finalize choices — Gina is on calendar for Wed afternoon US-PST.

Thanks — Carlos
